videos.title: 5 Common UI Design Patterns | Part 1
videos.why: Accordions, dropdowns, cards, breadcrumbs and the hamburger menu, each with when it helps; pause after each one and find a real example in an app you use.

videos.title: Tabs vs. Accordions: When to Use Each
videos.why: A clean rule of thumb, tabs for a few long sections and accordions for many short ones, plus what changes on mobile at 2:02; a model for choosing between two similar patterns.

podcasts.why: Two working interface designers talk through navigation patterns, the most common family of patterns in any app; compare what they describe with the navigation in your own product.
The person who coined 'dark patterns' explains the familiar patterns that are used to trick people, and how to avoid them; the other side of the idea that familiar patterns help users.

reads.title: Patterns
reads.why: Researched, tested patterns for asking for names, dates, addresses and passwords, checking answers and recovering from errors; open two or three and compare them with how your app does the same task.

reads.title: Modal & Nonmodal Dialogs: When (& When Not) to Use Them
reads.why: Modals interrupt and demand an action, so save them for information that truly needs attention; check every pop-up your AI tool has added against this article.

reads.title: Jakob's Law
reads.why: The one-line reason patterns matter, because people spend most of their time on other sites and expect yours to work the same way; read the takeaways before you invent a new control.
